done_when: no test creates, names or archives a thread in the user's real Codex home: every test that reaches Codex uses a throwaway Codex home, and a test run leaves the real home's thread list unchanged, proven by an end-to-end test

dismissals.because: tests/test_fix_codex_test_home.py:42 normal CI runners have no Codex login or real Codex home, so there is nothing there to pollute; the test runs wherever the pinned SDK is installed, which is every developer machine where the leak happened, and the codex-smoke workflow covers the real SDK

findings.body: The only end-to-end isolation test skips on a clean test runner because the pinned SDK is not installed. The normal suite workflows install only test dependencies (`.github/workflows/forge.yml:19–21` and `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:30–36`). The separate smoke workflow also skips execution when OPENAI_API_KEY is absent, so CI can pass without checking the required invariant. Under the explicit test-audit requirement, this proof must execute: provision its prerequisites in the suite or provide a runnable end-to-end test through Forge with third-party services faked at their edge.
findings.title: Not done: run the real-home isolation end-to-end test in the repository's test suite

why: Forge's test suite starts real Codex conversations in the user's own Codex home, so every test run leaves new threads in their Codex chat list
